correctness.rationale: The signed-axis polar plus diagonal apex representation follows from facet offsets; visible facets have exactly j>k positive signs, and summing precise outward pyramid determinants gives formula (1). Convexity of the spherical radial integral gives a unique Santaló minimizer. Differentiation gives the polynomial identity, while the one-corner equation and an O(2^{-n}/n) bound rigorously yield the displayed asymptotic. Exact code checks 141 grouped cases including hundreds of facet determinants, and independent SciPy hull comparisons in dimensions 2..6, corroborate without replacing proof.

value.rationale: The canonical uniform-matroid independence polytopes admit a full exact dual-volume function and thereby their algebraic Santaló volume products. The one-vertex cap is a natural high-dimensional perturbation of a cube whose Santaló center displacement is exponentially small with a sharp leading constant. This supplies a structural geometric sensitivity theorem, not a routine finite census.
